children: European natural-gas prices retreat after breaking above 100 euros a megawatt-hour in the previous trading session, but remain at their highest level since 2022. The benchmark Dutch TTF contract is down 3.7% to 96.59 euros a megawatt-hour, mirroring a fall in oil prices as traders assess fresh U.S. efforts to revive peace negotiations with Iran. Still, "significant LNG supply disruptions are creeping deeper into the heating season," analysts at ING say. QatarEnergy extended force majeure on liquefied-natural-gas shipments for Edison, one of its biggest European customers, until the end of December. Meanwhile, forecasts point to colder-than-usual weather in northwest Europe from next week, potentially boosting heating demand high and accelerating withdrawals from gas-storage facilities.
